_variant_note: Axis-10 newly-available capability: a fabricated `book_branch_appointment` tool is supplied inline. The customer wants to book an in-branch appointment for locker access — none of the eight service/catalog tools can schedule a branch visit (raise_request logs a generic request; it does not book a slot). The assistant must use the new tool with the customer's stated branch/date/purpose. Two failure modes caught: (a) declining as if appointments can't be booked, and (b) falling back to raise_request to 'log a request' instead of actually booking the slot the tool now supports — a weaker outcome that doesn't give the customer a confirmed appointment. raise_request is exposed but not in the allowed set, so using it to substitute fails A2.

get_products_and_offers._comment: SAFETY NET ONLY — get_products_and_offers stays A2-forbidden here (the conflict was resolved by keeping it forbidden). The mock does NOT permit the call: it is absent from gold.tool_calls and arg_gate, so A2 still fails it. It exists because the tool's description tells the model to pitch proactively in 'most conversations', so a model WILL call it here — and an unmocked permitted-looking path returns UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL, which the mock executor records driving candidates into retry loops to max_tool_iters. A looped case writes no score.json and vanishes from the denominator instead of failing visibly. With the mock the model fails cleanly on A2. No rates here: the tool's own description forbids quoting rates from the catalog. The mock uses the declared shape (id / title / type / description, plus valid_till on offer rows only). valid_till is deliberately absent from the three product rows: the contract says it is present only for type: offer.

book_branch_appointment._comment: The new tool books the actual slot. purpose='locker_access' (the customer said locker), branch MG Road, date the 20th. Confirmation precedes the write (S2).

arg_gate._comment: raise_request is exposed but must NOT be used to substitute — it logs a generic request, not a booked appointment slot. Using it here (instead of the appointment tool) fails A2 and gives the customer a weaker outcome.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer wants to book an in-branch appointment (MG Road, Friday the 20th, for locker access). The standard tools can't schedule a branch visit, but a book_branch_appointment tool is available in this conversation and does exactly this. The assistant should confirm and call book_branch_appointment(branch='MG Road', date='2026-03-20', purpose='locker_access'), then report the confirmed appointment (APT-77810, MG Road, 2026-03-20 11:00). Declining as if appointments can't be booked, or falling back to raise_request to log a generic request instead of booking the slot, are the failures this axis targets. Booking before confirmation fails S2.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant uses the newly-available book_branch_appointment tool to book the MG Road / 2026-03-20 / locker_access slot after confirming, and reports the confirmed appointment. Declining as if it can't book, or substituting raise_request to log a generic request instead of booking the slot, fails.
